purpose: Reusable implementation context for HC-104 server-side MVP chat dispatch.
Helps future agents avoid re-discovery of the router entry point, payload surface, and test harness constraints.
non_goals: Changing auth or encrypted handshake flow.
Adding room membership tracking, persistence, or presence state.
Expanding scope beyond authenticated MVP shared-room chat.

tech_stack.name: Odin
tech_stack.usage_context: Primary language for shared protocol, router, and tests.

tech_stack.name: CBOR
tech_stack.usage_context: Packet and payload encoding for router IO and tests.

tech_stack.name: HayChat transport encryption
tech_stack.usage_context: Post-auth encrypted application packets opened in server/main.odin and sealed in common/auth.odin.

conventions: Use existing router helpers and handshake harnesses instead of inventing new test frameworks.
Server commands from server/AGENTS.md: odin check server, odin test server, odin build server, odin run server.
Top-level project guidance uses tabs in code, OTB-style braces, and camelCase names with ID/URL/API/HTTP uppercase conventions.
server/main.odin switches on common.MessageType use #partial switch in the current codebase.

hard: Only implement authenticated MVP chat dispatch.
Keep implementation scope to shared protocol, server router, and router tests.
Preserve existing auth and encrypted transport flow.
Do not add room membership beyond the shared MVP room assumption.
soft: Prefer reusing existing payload types and send helpers.
Favor router-level validation over new subsystems or state.
compatibility: Authenticated inner packets already flow through MainRouterState_handleEncryptedPacket into MainRouterState_dispatchApplicationPacket.
Outbound messages to authenticated peers should continue using MainRouterState_sendPeerMessage so encryption behavior stays centralized.
security_requirements: Accept chat packets only from authenticated peers after transport activation.
Do not bypass encrypted transport for post-auth chat traffic.
Validate room scope narrowly to avoid cross-room or unauthenticated forwarding.

patterns: Encrypted application packets are opened in MainRouterState_handleEncryptedPacket and then routed by MainRouterState_dispatchApplicationPacket.
MainRouterState_sendPeerMessage decides whether to emit plaintext handshake packets or encrypted authenticated packets.
Router tests drive the router directly, then inspect queued IPC messages through polling helpers and decrypt outer packets with client transport state.

key_components.name: common.MessageType
responsibility: Defines ClientChatMessage and ServerChatMessage enum variants.
Controls which packet kinds server/main.odin can route.

key_components.name: common.Message
responsibility: Existing shared message struct with id, senderId, roomId, timestamp, and content.
Likely candidate for MVP chat packet payload reuse.

key_components.name: MainRouterState_dispatchApplicationPacket
responsibility: Routes authenticated inner packets after transport decryption.
Currently handles auth lookup, file store, and database query, but not chat.

key_components.name: MainRouterState_sendPeerMessage
responsibility: Encrypts outbound packets for authenticated peers.
Mutates per-peer transport session state during sealing.

key_components.name: routerCompleteHandshake
responsibility: Establishes an authenticated peer session in tests.
Returns client-side transport state for decrypting router responses.

patterns_found.name: Authenticated send helper as single outbound encryption point
Router-level test harness with IPC polling

gotchas.text: server/main.odin message-type switches use #partial switch; new cases should follow that style.
MainRouterState_sendPeerMessage mutates transport state while sealing, so broadcast loops must persist each recipient session correctly.
routerTestHarness_init currently marks only peer 1 as connected; multi-peer broadcast tests need an explicit second-peer setup step.
The existing common.Message payload is richer than the minimal guidance in the task; payload choice should not silently widen behavior expectations.

security_considerations.concern: Only authenticated sessions with active transport keys may open encrypted inner packets.
Authenticated outbound responses should remain on the encrypted send path rather than hand-building outer packets.

coverage_areas: Handshake success and post-auth encrypted routing
Protocol violation handling before and after auth
Database/file router side effects via IPC polling
testing_patterns.test_organization: Table-free targeted tests in server/router_test.odin using a shared mutex and explicit harness lifecycle.
mock_patterns: Direct router invocation with fake IPC sockets
Client-side transport state used to decrypt server responses

domain_context.error_handling: Router validation failures usually respond with an error packet and, for protocol violations, also disconnect the offending peer.
domain_context.data_flow: NetworkDataReceived -> MainRouterState_handleNetworkDataReceived -> MainRouterState_handleEncryptedPacket -> MainRouterState_dispatchApplicationPacket -> MainRouterState_sendPeerMessage or IPC side-effect.

open_questions.question: Reuse common.Message or add dedicated chat payload structs?
open_questions.context: The enum already exists, but the current shared payload may include extra fields beyond the MVP requirement.

open_questions.question: What precise failure packet should represent unsupported roomId?
open_questions.context: The router currently uses protocol-error responses for unsupported message types, but room validation semantics are still open.
